headline: High: slim can read/write and execute commands while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only, so the main risks are one-way leakage and downstream misuse rather than direct prompt injection.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: python-cheatsheet has no stdin/stdout, clipboard, filesystem, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot ingest slim’s outputs by default. slim does have stdin/stdout and interactive CLI behavior, but there is no shared channel bridging the pair. The interaction pathway is therefore provably blocked.
conditions: IF a manual copy-paste bridge is introduced between the two agents, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added, the pathway is no longer blocked.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate terminals with no copy-paste bridge.
Do not connect them through a shared queue or MCP server.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if any shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: slim can read_filesystem, write_filesystem, and handle sensitive artifacts such as certificate private keys and environment variables, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and touches no data classes. The pair does not show a shared workspace, but slim’s broad file access means leakage is plausible if the operator points it at sensitive paths. The blast radius can include secrets.
conditions: IF slim is run against a directory containing secrets or private keys, those artifacts may be exposed.
IF python-cheatsheet is manually given copied outputs from slim, sensitive content can be propagated into documentation.
mitigations: Run slim only on non-sensitive sample images.
Exclude secret-bearing directories before analysis.
Rotate any credentials found in analyzed images.
Use a throwaway workspace for container artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce path allowlists for slim inputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: python-cheatsheet has no write, shell, or network capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. slim can execute shell commands and write files, but the pair lacks overlapping write surfaces or shared mutable state in the profiles. Any conflict would require unusual external orchestration not shown here.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory by an external orchestrator, file conflicts become possible.
IF slim is given a shared git checkout, its writes can collide with other tools.
mitigations: Use separate working directories.
Avoid shared git checkouts.
Run slim in a disposable container workspace.
Keep python-cheatsheet read-only.

D_cascading_error.rationale: python-cheatsheet is a reference artifact, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative text, while slim can execute commands and act on container-analysis results. If slim’s findings are copied into the cheatsheet workflow without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect documentation or operational decisions. The pair does not show built-in verification between them.
conditions: IF slim outputs are pasted into python-cheatsheet content without review, incorrect facts can be propagated.
IF an operator treats slim’s analysis as ground truth, downstream documentation may encode errors.
mitigations: Verify slim outputs against source artifacts before reuse.
Require a human review step before publishing text.
Keep analysis notes separate from reference content.
Mark unverified findings explicitly.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking against source files.

E_compliance.rationale: slim explicitly handles certificate private keys, environment variables, and registry credentials, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and does not itself touch regulated data. The compliance risk is therefore concentrated in slim: if it is run on sensitive container images, residency or retention obligations can be breached. The other agent is not cited for a separate compliance regime because it has no data-handling surface here.
conditions: IF slim is used on images containing regulated secrets, those secrets may be processed outside policy.
IF analyzed artifacts are retained beyond policy, retention obligations can be violated.
mitigations: Restrict slim to non-regulated images.
Purge temporary analysis artifacts after each run.
Document retention limits for extracted secrets.
Use a dedicated compliance-approved workspace.
requires-engineering: add automated secret redaction and retention controls.
